newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House passes bill to reorganize patent agency.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House passes bill to reorganize patent agency.

text.p: The House of Representatives on Wednesday approved legislaton to make the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office an independent federal agency funded with application fees.
The office is now part of the Commerce Department.
The bill, which passed by voice vote, now goes to the Senate.
Patent applications from foreign inventors and companies would have to be filed in English, a new requirement.

The Clinton administration and other supporters of the bill said it would make the Patent Office more efficient. But opponents said the measure would make it easier for foreign businesses to steal U.S. intellectual property.

"The bill establishes the Patent and Trademark Office as a government corporation that will operate with greater flexibility on a daily basis," Commerce Secretary William Daley said in a letter to House members.
